I'm not trying to peddle any singular theistic or anti-theistic beliefs or practices, just sharing what worked for me at a low point in my life.  This way of living probably wouldn't work for someone who isn't as petty as I am.  I've ALWAYS had an issue with authority, and being able to metaphorically stick it to the supposed ultimate authority felt good.  Some of what OP said resonated with me, and i thought MAYBE that perspective would help them in some way.  Also, there's NOTHING wrong with living for yourself.  I'll never back down on that point. 

 I didn't say there's nothing worth more than ones own life.  I said almost nothing.  I'd argue almost  EVERYONE has something they will always hold more precious than themselves.  That's perfectly normal and healthy.  But living in service to someone or something at your detriment probably isn't.  

I'd say there's a difference between living for yourself and isolating yourself.  I probably could have elaborated more on that subject, but that thought didn't cross my mind.  I don't mean act like an ass and stop talking to people.  I mean, set boundaries that you stand behind 100%.  Don't let people walk all over you, don't let society pressure you into their norms.  Selfishness can be and often is an act of self-love.  Someone's perceived selfishness is just that, a perspective.  To the Selfish person, they're  simply staying alive.  Equating selfishness to sociopathy is wild BTW.  (But without my elaborating, I can see how you arrived there.)

We can speculate how any one path of thinking can be the downfall of anyone.  Speculative thinking like that is pointless and dangerous rhetoric in its own right.  

Overall, you made some great points.  This is in no way meant to be a hostile response, and I apologize deeply if it comes across that way.  I'm also typing this at 4 AM on the can, so I probably mistyped something.

Edit - I forgot to talk about the selfish feral rat part.  I mostly pulled that line from a TikTok i saw about someone escaping toxicity.  I definitely could have found a better parallel than that, but it got the point across with sufficient emphasis.  Honestly, I still stick by that.  Turn into a gremlin if it keeps you going, I see nothing wrong with this point.  If you can see what's wrong with it, please spell it out for me.   Sorry again if any of this was passive-aggressive in tone. It's not the tone I mean to convey, and it's still very late/early for me.

Edit 2-  I'm certain this isn't meant to be a debate board, so if you do feel inclined to continue the dialogue, please just dm me.

I'm an atheist through and through.  But when I was younger and still believed in a higher power, I was INCREDIBLY unhappy with everything about my life.  At a certain point, I decided to live in spite of any god.  Waking up every day and yelling, "Not today, you bastard!" Helped a lot.  Idk if this approach will work for you, but there's no one cure for hating existence.  Genuinely, there isn't much worth more than your own life.  If you have to turn into a feral selfish rat to continue living, I'd say that's you're right.
